kai: Noticed a new failure mode on the int8 canary: structured funcall outputs occasionally arrive as stitched partial JSON objects.

canary-bot: Canary alert: funcall_parse_fail_rate=7.9% (10m) for atlas-int8-bounty. https://canary.internal/atlas/bounty

maria: Paste one minimal concatenated example when you can.

kai: example (stream chunks joined): `{"action":"progress","args":{"step":2,"status":"ok"}

{"action":"notify","args":{"user":"u7","msg":"ready"}}` — missing close then new object.

ashley: Streaming + PTQ packing could be truncating mid-object. Did quant change eos or merge tokens?

devon: Short-term heuristic: parser tries greedy-last-object cut: find last '}' that yields valid top-level json; if found, emit repaired + repair_confidence. Reject repair if top-level action changes.

maria: Let's run a small token-id bounty: capture last 6 token ids for failed sessions (1% sample) and compare fp16 vs int8. If ids shift, flag PTQ tokenizer drift.

kai: Action items: @maria kick off token-id dumps; @ashley push parser-repair hook behind flag; @devon add repair_confidence + action_checksum metric. Pause int8 streaming canary if repairs spike >5%.

canary-bot: Scheduled grid: streaming on/off x kvcache reuse on/off x batch 1/2, sampling enabled. First results in ~30m.

kai: tl;dr: int8 streaming shows stitched JSONs. short-term: conservative repairs + telemetry. medium-term: token-id bisect vs fp16.
